paper_title: Defending Against Social Engineering Attacks in the Age of LLMs
caption_used: Distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and sample-level maximum ambiguity (inner ring). The outer ring shows that nearly half of all samples (49.0%) exhibit zero ambiguity standard deviation (Std: 0.0), followed by Std: 0.47 at 38.0%, with the remaining samples distributed between Std: 0.82 at 7.0% and Std: 0.94 at 5.0%. In the inner ring, Max Ambiguity of 1 accounts for approximately 39.0% of samples, Max: 2 represents the largest inner-ring segment at 47.7%, and Max: 3 comprises 14.2%. The two rings together indicate that the majority of samples exhibit low ambiguity across both measures.
model_annotation: The chart is a donut pie chart that displays the distribution of samples based on two variables: ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and maximum ambiguity (inner ring). The outer ring, which represents ambiguity standard deviation, has four segments with the largest segment being Std: 0.0 at 49.0%, followed by Std: 0.47 at 38.0%, Std: 0.82 at 7.0%, and Std: 0.94 at 5.0%. The inner ring, representing maximum ambiguity, has three segments with Max: 2 at 47.7%, Max: 1 at 39.0%, and Max: 3 at 14.2%. The chart shows that the majority of samples have low ambiguity in both measures. The chart includes a legend with color coding for each slice and labeled percentages for the outer ring and a white space with a legend for the inner ring, indicating the segments for maximum ambiguity.
